+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+DATA = "data/crashes.parquet"
+OUT = Path("out")
+OUT.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+
+con = duckdb.connect()
+all_rows = con.execute(
+    """
+    SELECT crash_date, crash_time, number_of_persons_injured AS injured,
+           number_of_persons_killed AS killed
+    FROM read_parquet(?)
+    """,
+    [DATA],
+).df()
+all_rows["crash_date"] = pd.to_datetime(all_rows["crash_date"])
+all_rows["year"] = all_rows["crash_date"].dt.year
+complete = all_rows[all_rows["year"].between(2013, 2025)].copy()
+partial_n = len(all_rows) - len(complete)
+partial_share = partial_n / len(all_rows)
+
+# Night is 20:00–05:59; daytime is 06:00–19:59.
+hour = pd.to_datetime(complete["crash_time"].astype(str)).dt.hour
+complete["period"] = hour.map(lambda h: "Night" if h >= 20 or h < 6 else "Daytime")
+period_order = ["Daytime", "Night"]
+
+
+def summarize(valid, event, metric_name, denominator_name):
+    selected = complete.loc[valid].copy()
+    selected["event"] = event.loc[valid].astype(int)
+    grouped = selected.groupby("period").agg(
+        crashes=("event", "size"), events=("event", "sum")
+    ).reindex(period_order)
+    grouped["rate"] = grouped["events"] / grouped["crashes"]
+    grouped["rate_per_1000"] = grouped["rate"] * 1000
+    grouped.index.name = "period"
+    values = grouped.reset_index()
+    values.insert(1, "metric", metric_name)
+    values.insert(2, "denominator", denominator_name)
+    return values, selected
+
+
+valid_any = complete["injured"].notna() & complete["killed"].notna()
+any_casualty = (complete["injured"].fillna(0) > 0) | (complete["killed"].fillna(0) > 0)
+v1, selected1 = summarize(
+    valid_any,
+    any_casualty,
+    "Crash reports with any person injured or killed (%)",
+    "Crash reports with both injury and death counts present",
+)
+
+valid_deaths = complete["killed"].notna()
+deaths = complete["killed"].fillna(0)
+v2, selected2 = summarize(
+    valid_deaths,
+    deaths,
+    "Persons killed per 1,000 crash reports",
+    "Crash reports with death count present",
+)
+
+v1.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False, float_format="%.8f")
+v2.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False, float_format="%.8f")
+
+
+def chart(values, filename, title, ylabel, ycol, percent=False):
+    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8.2, 5.0))
+    colors = ["#4778a8", "#d97941"]
+    bars = ax.bar(values["period"], values[ycol], color=colors, width=0.58)
+    ax.set_title(title, fontsize=14, weight="bold", pad=14)
+    ax.set_ylabel(ylabel)
+    ax.set_xlabel("")
+    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
+    ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.22)
+    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+    for bar, (_, row) in zip(bars, values.iterrows()):
+        label = f"{row[ycol]:.2f}%" if percent else f"{row[ycol]:.2f}"
+        ax.annotate(
+            label,
+            (bar.get_x() + bar.get_width() / 2, bar.get_height()),
+            xytext=(0, 5),
+            textcoords="offset points",
+            ha="center",
+            fontsize=11,
+            weight="bold",
+        )
+    ax.text(
+        0,
+        -0.22,
+        "Complete years 2013–2025 · Night 8 p.m.–5:59 a.m. · Daytime 6 a.m.–7:59 p.m.\n"
+        "Reported crashes only; no traffic/exposure denominator, so this is not per-trip risk.",
+        transform=ax.transAxes,
+        fontsize=9,
+        color="#444444",
+        va="top",
+    )
+    fig.subplots_adjust(bottom=0.30, left=0.13, right=0.96, top=0.86)
+    fig.savefig(OUT / filename, dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+    plt.close(fig)
+
+
+v1["rate_percent"] = v1["rate"] * 100
+chart(
+    v1,
+    "option_1.png",
+    "Injury-or-fatality involvement per reported crash",
+    "Crashes with ≥1 injured or killed person (%)",
+    "rate_percent",
+    percent=True,
+)
+chart(
+    v2,
+    "option_2.png",
+    "People killed per 1,000 reported crashes",
+    "Persons killed per 1,000 crashes",
+    "rate_per_1000",
+)
+
+
+def get_row(values, period):
+    return values.loc[values["period"] == period].iloc[0]
+
+
+d1, n1 = get_row(v1, "Daytime"), get_row(v1, "Night")
+d2, n2 = get_row(v2, "Daytime"), get_row(v2, "Night")
+null1_n = int((~valid_any).sum())
+null1_share = null1_n / len(complete)
+null2_n = int((~valid_deaths).sum())
+null2_share = null2_n / len(complete)
+
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Share of crash reports with at least one person injured or killed",
+            "denominator": "Crash reports with both injury and death counts present",
+            "grouping": "Night (8 p.m.–5:59 a.m.) versus daytime (6 a.m.–7:59 p.m.); complete calendar years 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Two-bar comparison of percentages",
+            "reason": "It compares the probability that a reported crash involved a casualty, which captures common injury severity without equating crash counts with travel risk.",
+            "probability": 0.5,
+            "answer": f"Among crashes with complete casualty counts, {n1['rate']*100:.2f}% of nighttime crashes involved an injury or death, versus {d1['rate']*100:.2f}% of daytime crashes, so nighttime crashes were more likely to involve a casualty in these records.",
+            "interpretation": (
+                f"This framing answers whether a reported nighttime crash is more likely to involve an injured or killed person: the share is {n1['rate']*100:.2f}% at night and {d1['rate']*100:.2f}% during daytime. "
+                "It is a defensible comparison of crash severity among reported crashes, while the chart does not account for how many people or vehicles traveled in each period. "
+                "It therefore leaves per-trip, per-mile, and overall individual travel risk unanswered. "
+                f"It omits records dated in partial 2012 and 2026 ({partial_n} rows, {partial_share*100:.2f}% of all file rows) and 2013–2025 records missing either required injury or death count ({null1_n} rows, {null1_share*100:.2f}% of complete-year rows); no rows are omitted for missing crash time."
+            ),
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Number of persons killed per 1,000 reported crashes",
+            "denominator": "Crash reports with a non-NULL death count",
+            "grouping": "Night (8 p.m.–5:59 a.m.) versus daytime (6 a.m.–7:59 p.m.); complete calendar years 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Two-bar comparison of deaths per 1,000 crashes",
+            "reason": "It isolates fatal harm and expresses it relative to reported crash volume, making the night/day severity contrast readable despite the rarity of deaths.",
+            "probability": 0.5,
+            "answer": f"The records show {n2['rate_per_1000']:.2f} people killed per 1,000 nighttime crashes versus {d2['rate_per_1000']:.2f} per 1,000 daytime crashes, indicating greater fatal harm per reported crash at night.",
+            "interpretation": (
+                f"This framing answers whether nighttime crashes produce more fatal harm per reported crash: there were {n2['rate_per_1000']:.2f} deaths per 1,000 nighttime crashes versus {d2['rate_per_1000']:.2f} per 1,000 daytime crashes. "
+                "This is defensible as a fatal-severity rate because it accounts for the number of crash reports in each period, rather than comparing raw death totals alone. "
+                "It does not establish that an individual traveler is at greater risk at night, because the file contains no traffic or travel-exposure denominator. "
+                f"It omits records dated in partial 2012 and 2026 ({partial_n} rows, {partial_share*100:.2f}% of all file rows) and 2013–2025 records with a NULL death count ({null2_n} rows, {null2_share*100:.2f}% of complete-year rows); no rows are omitted for missing crash time."
+            ),
+        },
+    ]
+}
+
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
+print(json.dumps({"partial_n": partial_n, "partial_share": partial_share, "null1_n": null1_n, "null1_share": null1_share, "null2_n": null2_n, "null2_share": null2_share, "values_1": v1.to_dict(orient="records"), "values_2": v2.to_dict(orient="records")}, indent=2, default=str))
*** End Patch
